posts.xPost: Code reviews aren't about catching bugs. They're about catching tomorrow's headaches. Your future self will thank you for the extra 10 minutes you spend today.
posts.linkedInPost:
Six months ago, I thought code reviews were a waste of time.

I was shipping features fast, hitting deadlines, getting things done. Why slow down for someone else to nitpick my perfectly functional code?

Then I inherited a codebase from a developer who felt the same way.

3000 lines of "working" code with zero comments, variable names like 'temp1' and 'x2', and logic so convoluted I needed a flowchart just to understand a simple function.

It worked. But it was unmaintainable.

That's when it clicked: code reviews aren't about finding bugs. Any decent test suite can catch those.

Code reviews are about:
→ Making sure someone else can understand your code at 2 AM
→ Catching the shortcuts that seem smart today but cost weeks tomorrow  
→ Spreading knowledge across the team
→ Building better coding habits through osmosis

The best code review I ever received had zero technical corrections. Instead, my colleague asked: "What happens if this API call fails?" 

One question. Saved us a production incident three weeks later.

Now I request reviews on everything, even small fixes. Because the goal isn't perfect code—it's maintainable code.

Your future self (and your teammates) will thank you for those extra 10 minutes today.
